title: HSS — Strength Training for Teens: What to Know
summary: Strength training is safe for teens (and pre-adolescents) when supervised by a trained professional. Use age-appropriate exercises, proper movement patterns, major muscle groups + core, and slow progression. 2–3 sessions/week on nonconsecutive days, 3 sets of 10–15 reps at manageable weight. Never attempt a 1-rep max. Dynamic warmup 5–10 min. Avoid performance supplements.
guardrail_reason: Strength prescriptions must include supervision requirement and forbid 1RM in minors.
coach_use_case: Source of truth for teen strength rules.

title: GSSI — The Healthy Youth Athlete: Hydration
summary: Hydration supports cognition, heat safety, and performance. Adolescent sweat rates exceed 1 L/h; mature adolescents can hit 2.5 L/h+. Avoid >2-3% body-mass deficit. Use body-weight change pre/post practice and first-morning urine color as practical estimators. Be more conservative with multi-session/heat days.
guardrail_reason: Hydration guidance — not clinical hydration treatment.
